[.claude/CLAUDE.md#project-overview]

## Project Overview

**Polyglot** Enterprise Architecture project for Gainwell Technologies. Supports Python, C#, Java, Rust, React/Next.js, and Terraform. Provides document conversion tools, automated developer onboarding, shared branding/styling, IaC scaffolding, and AI-assisted workflows.

See [README.md](../README.md) for the full overview.
page_texts.3:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#setup]

## Setup

Use [Task](https://taskfile.dev) for all build, test, and deployment operations:

```bash
task setup          # Bootstrap all environments (Python, and components as created)
task health         # Check that all required tools are installed
task lint           # Run all linters (Python, Markdown, Terraform, components)
task test           # Run all tests across all languages
task ci             # Run full CI pipeline locally
```
page_texts.4:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#python-setup-for-utils]

### Python Setup (for .utils/)

**pip + venv** — NOT Poetry.

- Shared virtual environment: `.utils/.venv/`
- Dependencies: `.utils/requirements.txt`
- All conversion tools share the same environment
- Managed via `task utils:setup` (or `task setup` at root)

```bash
task utils:setup              # Bootstrap Python environment
task utils:setup:force        # Re-create from scratch
```
page_texts.5:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#structure]

## Structure

```text
.assets/              Logos, stylesheets (Gainwell branding)
.claude/              Claude Code config, commands, skills
.github/              GitHub config, Copilot instructions, CI/CD workflows
.utils/               Python environment + document conversion tools
  Taskfile.yml        Python-specific tasks (setup, lint, test, format)
  formatters/         7 converters (md2pdf, md2docx, docx2md, pdf2md, pptx2md, pptx2pdf, xlsx2md)
.vscode/              Shared VS Code workspace settings
docs/                 Documentation (conceptual, logical, physical, requirements)
onboarding/           Platform setup scripts (macOS + Windows)
.tooling/              Legacy publication-tooling subsystem (components + IaC) — pending removal from this repo, self-governed (see .tooling/README.md); not part of the EA-documentation Skill catalog
.tmp/                 Scratch / temporary files (gitignored)
Taskfile.yml          Root orchestrator for all languages and tools
.project.yml          Project config (coverage thresholds per language, project type)
```
page_texts.6:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#document-conversion-tools]

## Document Conversion Tools

All in `.utils/formatters/`, managed via Task commands:

```bash
task convert:md2pdf -- file.md           # Markdown → PDF
task convert:md2docx -- file.md          # Markdown → Word
task convert:docx2md -- file.docx        # Word → Markdown
task convert:pdf2md -- file.pdf          # PDF → Markdown
task convert:pptx2md -- file.pptx        # PowerPoint → Markdown
task convert:pptx2pdf -- file.pptx       # PowerPoint → PDF
task convert:xlsx2md -- file.xlsx        # Excel → Markdown
```

Or directly via Python:

```bash
python .utils/formatters/md2pdf/md2pdf.py file.md -o output.pdf -v
```
page_texts.7:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#conventions]

## Conventions

- **Task runner**: Use `task` for all build/test/lint operations (never run language-specific commands directly in CI)
- **Python 3.13+** required for `.utils/` tools
- **Run from repo root** — never cd into tool directories
- **Relative paths only** — no hardcoded absolute paths
- **All documentation in Markdown**
- **Keep setup scripts in sync**: `onboarding/setup-mac.sh` and `onboarding/setup-windows.ps1`
- **Branding via** `.assets/stylesheets/`
- **`.tmp/` for scratch work** — never commit content there
- **Python formatting**: black (line-length 100), ruff, mypy — configs in `.utils/pyproject.toml`

[.claude/CLAUDE.md#skill-invocation-transparency]

## Skill Invocation Transparency

When fulfilling a user request, **always announce which skills will be involved** before starting work. This makes the workflow visible so the user can track what's happening.
page_texts.9:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#how-to-announce]

### How to announce

At the start of any non-trivial request, output a brief skill plan:

```text
**Skills involved:**
- `/business-analyst` — identify requirements scope
- `/architect` — design the bounded context
- `/documenter` — write the artifact content
- `/ea-reviewer` — verify EA compliance
```
page_texts.10:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#when-to-announce]

### When to announce

- **Always** for any project-related request — this is the default. Every response to a project task must start with the skills list before any other output.
- **Always** when more than one skill will be invoked
- **Always** when the request spans requirements, design, implementation, or testing
- **Skip** only for general questions not related to the project (e.g., "what is pipefail", "explain this concept")
page_texts.11:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#the-13-core-skills-and-their-job-duties]

### The 13 core skills and their job duties

| Skill | Job Duty | Owns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **business-analyst** | Elicits and defines requirements, guides domain language | `docs/requirements/`, traceability matrix |
| **architect** | Designs solutions, sets patterns, governs standards — uses `/modeler` for diagrams | `docs/decisions/`, enterprise compliance |
| **enterprise-architect** | Decides which EA artifact type (ADR, Pattern, Standard, Guidance, Reference Architecture, White Paper) an outcome needs, and judges authoring/maintenance quality — used by `ea-author` | Artifact-type recommendation, authoring judgment |
| **ai-architect** | Decides which AI construct type (Skill, Agent, Workflow, Instruction, Rule) a repository need requires, and judges authoring/maintenance quality — used by `ai-author` | Construct-type recommendation, authoring judgment |
| **ea-reviewer** | Reviews EA artifact changes (standards, patterns, guidance, ADRs, white papers) in PRs/diffs — gates merges | Approve/Request Changes verdict |
| **ai-reviewer** | Reviews AI construct changes (Skills, Agents, Workflows/Commands/Prompts, Instructions, file-pattern Instructions) in PRs/diffs — gates merges | Approve/Request Changes verdict |
| **ai-convergence** | Simulates a peer AI reviewer's cold read before commit — closes consistency gaps | Pre-commit convergence report |
| **diagrammer** | Routes diagram requests to `/modeler` or `/presenter` based on intent | Diagram routing |
| **modeler** | Architecture + data model diagrams — Mermaid (default), Draw.io (complex) | Technical diagrams, ER models |
| **presenter** | Deck-ready presentation visuals — Draw.io, 16:9, full style guide | `assets/` deck diagrams, SVG exports |
| **documenter** | Writes and maintains all documentation and glossaries | `docs/` content, glossary files |
| **project-manager** | Tracks progress, milestones, risks, decisions | `docs/project-plan.md` |
| **tech-evaluator** | Runs structured COTS/SaaS/OSS technology evaluations using the PES framework | `strategy/tech-evals/`, scored comparisons |
page_texts.12:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#collaboration-rules]

### Collaboration rules

- **BA and architect guide, documenter writes** — glossary and documentation
- **`ea-reviewer` vs `ai-reviewer`** — `ea-reviewer` gates EA artifact changes (standards, patterns, guidance, ADRs, white papers). For AI construct changes (Skills, Agents, Workflows/Commands/Prompts, Instructions, file-pattern Instructions), use `.claude/skills/ai-reviewer/SKILL.md` via the `@ai-author`/`@ai-review` Agents instead — not this skill.
- **Diagrammer owns all visuals** — documenter and architect delegate diagram creation to `/diagrammer`
- **Documenter cascades to diagrammer** — after modifying a markdown file, `/documenter` invokes `/diagrammer --cascade <path>` to detect and update any `.drawio` files whose `sourceMarkdown` attribute matches the changed file
- **ai-convergence runs before commit when another AI reviews** — after any documenter or architect pass that will be reviewed by a peer AI (Copilot, second Claude) and is not a trivial single-line fix with no logical parallel elsewhere (see the Skill's trivial-fix exclusion), invoke `/ai-convergence` before `/eap-git` or `/eap-push` to close parallel-statement and prose-to-structure gaps
- **All skills read the glossary** — only documenter writes to it

[.claude/CLAUDE.md#glossary-structure]

## Glossary Structure

The project uses a two-tier glossary for ubiquitous language:

| Tier | Location | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Project-wide** | `docs/glossary.md` | Cross-cutting terms (Medicaid, healthcare industry, platform architecture) |
| **Domain-specific** | `docs/design/conceptual/domains/<domain>/glossary.md` | Terms owned by a single bounded context |

- Domain-specific terms go in the domain glossary
- Cross-cutting terms go in the project-wide glossary
- The **documenter** skill is the primary glossary maintainer, guided by **business-analyst** and **architect**

[.claude/CLAUDE.md#do-not]

## Do NOT

- **Add Poetry** — we use pip+venv for Python
- **Create separate venvs per tool** — use the shared `.utils/.venv`
- **Put Python files in repo root** — keep in `.utils/`
- **Hard-code absolute paths**
- **Commit to `.tmp/`**
- **Override `.vscode/settings.json`** for personal preferences

[.claude/CLAUDE.md#adding-a-new-component]

## Adding a New Component

1. Create `components/<component-name>/` with:
   - `src/` — source code
   - `tests/` — tests
   - `Taskfile.yml` — component-specific tasks (build, test, lint, clean)
   - `README.md` — purpose, language/framework, setup, usage
   - Language-specific project files (e.g., `*.csproj`, `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`)
2. Update root `Taskfile.yml` to include the new component:

   ```yaml
   includes:
     mycomponent:
       taskfile: components/mycomponent/Taskfile.yml
       dir: components/mycomponent
   ```

3. Add component-specific tasks to root orchestrator (test, lint, clean, etc.)
4. Update `.project.yml` coverage thresholds if needed
5. Test with `task <component>:test` and `task ci`
page_texts.16:
[.claude/CLAUDE.md#adding-a-new-python-conversion-tool]

## Adding a New Python Conversion Tool

1. Create `.utils/formatters/<newtool>/` with Python script + `README.md`
2. Follow CLI pattern: argparse with input, `-o/--output`, `-v/--verbose`
3. Add deps to `.utils/requirements.txt`
4. Add task to `.utils/Taskfile.yml` under `convert:<tool>`
5. Add task to root `Taskfile.yml` to delegate to `.utils/Taskfile.yml`
6. Update README.md
7. Test with shared venv: `task utils:setup` and `task convert:<tool> -- <file>`

[.claude/CLAUDE.md#enterprise-reference-architecture]

## Enterprise Reference Architecture

The `eap-ref-architecture` repo is the single source of truth for enterprise architecture guidance. Always consult it before creating new patterns, standards, or architecture artifacts.

Key locations:

- `standards/` — mandatory technical standards by domain (API, security, Python, Next.js, EKS, Kafka, etc.)
- `patterns/` — reusable architectural patterns by domain
- `decisions/` — enterprise-level ADRs by domain
- `guiding-principles/` — core and domain-specific principles
- `strategy/` — best practices, guidance, reference architectures, white papers
- `governance/` — processes, committees, metrics
- `resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/` — templates for ADRs, patterns, standards, RCAs, white papers, and more

**Content Taxonomy:**

| Type          | Purpose                                                                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Patterns**  | Define **HOW** to solve common problems — reusable architectural solutions            |
| **Standards** | Define **WHAT** must be done — mandatory requirements teams must meet                 |
| **Guidance**  | Define **WHY** and **HOW TO IMPLEMENT** — step-by-step implementation approaches      |

**Security Routing Exception:**
Security content defaults to `strategy/guidance/security/`, but this default is not absolute: technical implementation patterns (e.g., OAuth2 flows, Kubernetes security controls) belong in `patterns/security/`, and compliance-baseline standards with independently auditable scope belong in `standards/security/`. Only when the content is genuinely ambiguous or spans the boundary between these types does it default to `strategy/guidance/security/`. See `.claude/commands/guidance.md`, `.claude/commands/pattern.md`, and `.claude/commands/standard.md` for the full classification rule.

Content is organized across 8 domains: Application, Business, Governance, Information, Infrastructure, ITSM-Operations, Security, Technology.

**Do not duplicate enterprise content into this repo — link to it instead.**

[.claude/CLAUDE.md#workflow-commands]

## Workflow Commands

Reusable workflow instructions are in `.claude/commands/`. Read the relevant command file before performing these operations:

- **Activity brief** (`.claude/commands/activity-brief.md`) — Synthesize an audience-scoped outcomes brief from one person's Azure Boards and GitHub activity over a date range. Outputs an evidence/inference trail and a leadership-ready outcomes brief (no individual attribution). Invoke with `assignee=<ado-email> author=<github-login> range=<start:end>`. Add `--slide` to also produce a 1-slide deck via `/presenter`.
